threatens substantially to interrupt in­

to deprive a large section of the country 
of essential transportation service:
NOW, THEREFORE by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by section 10 of 
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45
U. S. C. 160), I hereby create a board of 
three members, to be appointed by me, 
to investigate the said dispute. No mem­
ber of the said board shall be pecuniarily

dispute within thirty days from the date 
of this order.

date and for thirty days after the board 
has made its report to the President, no 
change, except by agreement, shall be 
made by the Northwest Airlines, Inc., or 
its employees in the conditions out of 
which the said dispute arose.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The order ended by its own terms on 1949-04-09, inclusive. Its last-running command is the standstill: from the date of the order, January 19, 1949, and for thirty days after the board has made its report to the President, no change except by agreement is to be made by Northwest Airlines, Inc., or its employees in the conditions out of which the dispute arose. The board's signed letter submitting its report to the President is dated 1949-03-10 according to the reviewed factual-event record recorded as a later event; I count the report as made on that date, so the thirty days after it end on April 9, 1949, and the order was spent from the end of that day. The exclusive reading, under which the standstill ends when April 9 begins, is the alternative. The held sources show the date of the letter and do not show when it reached the White House, so the date assumes the report was made when submitted. The report requirement (due within thirty days of the order, extended thirty days by an order of February 11, 1949 that the board's letter mentions but that is not held) was performed by that submission, and the creation of the board was carried out by its appointment on January 24, 1949. Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237), later revoked the order by number as one of the orders listed in its table, with no saving clause; that revocation came after the end recorded here and is a later event, not the first end, because the order had already run out under its own terms.

research_rationale:
Identity: the held Federal Register text (14 FR 289, issue of January 20, 1949, PDF page 1) is the order itself: it is headed Executive Order 10029, creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate the dispute between Northwest Airlines, Inc., and certain of its employees represented by the International Association of Machinists, and is signed by Harry S. Truman at The White House on January 19, 1949. I read the whole order; the representation is the machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF, and I did not inspect the page images. End: the last-running command of the order is its standstill, which runs from the date of the order until thirty days after the board has made its report to the President. A reviewed factual-event record (an independent AI factual review by a reviewer of the same model family as its producer, not a human review) gives 1949-03-10 as the date of the board's signed transmittal letter submitting its report to the President. The letter names Executive Order 10029 of January 19, 1949 and the board's appointment on January 24, 1949, and the board states in it that it submits its report. The held OCR text of the letter garbles the month of its dateline, so the month comes from the reviewer's visual inspection of the page image recorded in the event; it is consistent with the letter's own chronology, because the letter says the board's time was extended thirty days by an order dated February 11, 1949, which moves the report deadline from February 18, 1949 (thirty days after January 19) to March 20, 1949, and March 10 falls inside that period. The extension order itself is not held, and the extension is not claimed as an end. I count the report as made when the board submitted it, on the letter date, so the thirty days after it end on 1949-04-09 (1949 is not a leap year: March 10 plus 30 days is April 9). Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on until-dates the end is recorded inclusive, so the standstill runs through the end of April 9, 1949; the exclusive reading ends it when that day begins. The held sources do not show when the letter reached the White House; if the standstill ran only from receipt, it ended later by the delivery time, and this claim does not establish that interval. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 revoked the order formally; under the owner ruling of 2026-10-28 that later cleanup revocation is recorded as a later event with its own date and is not the first end. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete with no coverage warning and no scope note; the U.S. Code and eCFR searches found no hit naming this order, and the Federal Register catalog search reports two hits for it while the dossier chain locates one instrument, Executive Order 12553. A search of the held order texts for the number found only the order's own Federal Register text. Prior research: a filed claim by agent claude (research/readiness/claims/claude-2026-10-31-apollo-g03.jsonl) ended the order on 1986-02-25 and a later retag recorded that date only as a not-later-than bound; this claim replaces it with the own-terms end and keeps the revocation as a later event.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"The order contains no fixed end date and no termination clause. Its commands are the creation of a board of three members, a bar on members interested in any organization of employees or any carrier, a requirement that the board report within thirty days from the date of the order (due February 18, 1949 before the extension the board's letter mentions), and a standstill from the date of the order until thirty days after the board has made its report. The report deadline is a deadline and is not claimed as an end; the end claimed is the expiry of the standstill under the order's own terms, thirty days after the dated submission of the report. The dossier chain, the three machine searches and my reading of the held text of Executive Order 12553 show no revoking, superseding or amending instrument before 1986-02-25. The board's letter says the board was appointed on January 24, 1949 and that its time was extended thirty days by an order dated February 11, 1949; that order is not held and it moves only the report deadline. The retained annual-report text that the factual reviewer mentions reads thirty-six days in one place where the report images read thirty; the review records that the duration is unresolved and accepts no extension duration, and the end claimed here does not depend on it.","independent_command_check":"Each command (create the board, bar interested members, require the report, freeze conditions) depends on this order and on the dispute it created; none is a separate delegation, continuing regulation or standing rule. The standstill sentence applies section 10 of the Railway Labor Act (45 U.S.C. 160); the statute is a separate source of law that an Executive order does not revoke, but the thirty-day period it measures here was set by this order's creation of the board and ended by its own terms on 1949-04-09.","savings_check":"Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 was read in full: it consists of an enacting sentence revoking the listed orders and any amendments to them, a table of the revoked orders by number and subject, and the signature block, and it contains no saving or transition provision. No residual effect of Executive Order 10029 is shown to depend on its continued force after the standstill ended on 1949-04-09; section 10 of the Railway Labor Act continues independently of this order.","scope_check":"One clause is inventoried: the operative text from the order heading through the standstill sentence, comprising the recitals, the creation of the board of three members, the bar on interested members, the thirty-day report requirement and the standstill. The signature and date line follow it and contain no command. Executive Order 12553 revokes the order by number as a whole, not in part. Of the commands, the creation of the board was carried out by the appointment of the board on January 24, 1949 as the board's letter states, and the report requirement was performed by the submission of the report on the letter date. The bar on interested members has no end stated in the order; it applies to the members of this board, and no held source assigns the board any task after its report, so I treat it as spent no later than the end of the standstill, which is the latest dated command. That treatment is an inference, since the date the board was discharged is not shown by any held source."}

savings_residuals.reason: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 was read in full: it consists of an enacting sentence revoking the listed orders and any amendments to them, a table of the revoked orders by number and subject, and the signature block, and it contains no saving or transition provision. No residual effect of Executive Order 10029 is shown to depend on its continued force after the standstill ended on 1949-04-09; section 10 of the Railway Labor Act continues independently of this order.
